hints: Focus on the gas that is actually released in each mixture, then ask yourself if that gas is acidic, alkaline or neutral.
Remember the classic test reactions: ammonium salt plus base gives ammonia, metal plus acid gives hydrogen, and solid chloride plus concentrated sulfuric acid gives hydrogen chloride.
Decide which of ammonia, hydrogen and hydrogen chloride turns damp blue litmus red, and you will have found the acidic gas.
walkthrough:
**What counts as an acidic gas?**

An acidic gas dissolves in water to give an acidic solution and turns damp blue litmus paper red. Good examples are $\text{HCl}$, $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{NO}_2$. In contrast, $\text{NH}_3$ is alkaline and $\text{H}_2$ is neutral.

Rule to use:
$$\text{acidic gas} + \text{water} \rightarrow \text{acidic solution}$$

**Work out the gas from each mixture**

For A, ammonium ions with base (from $\text{CaO}$ in water) give ammonia:
$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
For B, a metal with an acid gives hydrogen:
$$\text{Ca} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
For C, a solid chloride with concentrated sulfuric acid gives hydrogen chloride:
$$\text{KCl} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{KHSO}_4 + \text{HCl}$$
For D, a basic oxide with water gives only a solution, no gas:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$

**Classify each product**

$\text{NH}_3$ from A is an alkaline gas. $\text{H}_2$ from B is a neutral gas. No gas at all forms in D, only aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Only $\text{HCl}$ from C is a classic acidic gas, forming hydrochloric acid in water.

options.A: Aqueous ammonium nitrate provides NH4+ and calcium oxide in water provides OH-. They react to release ammonia, NH3, which is an alkaline gas that turns damp red litmus blue, not an acidic gas.
options.B: Calcium is a reactive metal, so with aqueous HCl it gives calcium chloride and hydrogen gas, H2. Hydrogen is neutral and does not turn litmus, so this is a common trap if you see an acid and assume the gas must be acidic.
options.C: Solid potassium chloride with concentrated sulfuric acid is the standard laboratory preparation of hydrogen chloride gas, HCl. HCl dissolves to give a strong acid and turns damp blue litmus red, so it is the acidic gas required.
options.D: Sodium oxide is a basic oxide and simply dissolves in water to give sodium hydroxide solution, NaOH. No gas is evolved at all, so it cannot be an acidic gas.
